summary:
We developed Satellite Launch, an interactive simulation game where players act as space engineers to design, manage, and launch a satellite into orbit.
Players make critical engineering decisions on satellite weight, fuel amount, and orbit height while managing limited fuel resources. Choosing a light satellite saves fuel but gives a weak signal, while a heavy satellite gives a strong signal but risks fuel depletion.
This game addresses the challenge by teaching resource management and trade-off evaluation, the core of real space missions. It is important because it makes space engineering accessible and fun, helping students understand that every choice in space shapes mission success.
details: We developed an interactive game called Satellite Launch where the player acts as a space engineer to design, manage, and simulate a complete satellite launch mission while making critical engineering decisions about satellite weight, fuel amount, and orbit height under limited fuel resources. The game works by letting players choose between a light satellite that needs less fuel but sends weak signals and a heavy satellite that needs more fuel but sends strong signals, and as the satellite ascends fuel decreases in real time, so if fuel runs out before reaching orbit the mission fails but if fuel remains the mission succeeds and signal strength is evaluated. The benefit is that it teaches resource management and engineering trade-offs in a fun and simple way, and its intended impact is to make space engineering accessible to students and inspire interest in real space missions. We built the project using Scratch block-based coding with variables for Fuel and Signal Strength, ask-and-wait blocks for decisions, repeat loops for launch simulation, and if-else conditions for success evaluation.
